How much should you risk per trade? 📉

Two traders can run the exact same strategy and end up in completely different places. The difference is the size of each bet.

In our (hypothetical) simulation, a strategy with the same +0.2R edge per trade had a median max drawdown of 15% at 1% risk per trade, and 89% at 10%. At 20%, nearly half the runs lost money.

New on the blog:
• fixed-fractional sizing in one formula
• why losing streaks of 10+ are normal, even for a strategy with a positive edge
• the Kelly criterion, and why traders bet less than it says
• what happens when your real edge is smaller than your backtest
• a practical checklist before you pick a risk %
